items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).
tags: LLM agents; cyber deception; network security

items.summary: This edition presents the current Split-Zero, theta-cohomology and arithmetic-kernel calculations in a research programme on the Riemann zeta function. It publishes the complete 216-page cumulative continuation, the updated 425-page broader research reader, and their proof sources and checks. The purpose is to make the actual calculations readable and reproducible: what was attempted, why that route was chosen, the maps and estimates obtained, and the precise points where the argument remains unfinished. Start with the cumulative calculation reader 14-splitzero-tau-kernel-continuation.pdf is the primary preview. Its 22 proof sections and nine complete source appendices carry the programme from Split-Zero coefficients through theta cohomology, interpolation kernels, chain retractions, homotopy control and the symmetric arithmetic frontier. Earlier source notes retain their own revisions and attribution; the cumulative continuation is not presented as though all its source results originated in one session. Split-Zero coefficients keep the original zero of a ring as a supported element and adjoin a different, external zero, tau. This records the difference between cancelling a coefficient and forgetting the fibre that carried it. Theta cohomology is a specified space of rapidly decreasing functions modulo the image of a specified theta-summation map. Under the stated Mellin transform, that map becomes multiplication by g(s) = 2 xi(s) , where xi is the completed Riemann zeta function. A finite spectral packet records spectral points with their multiplicities, using polynomial quotients and full derivative data rather than discarding repeated-root directions. The calculations construct minimum-norm representatives from the original arithmetic measure, derive full-jet kernel and Gram-inverse formulas, follow nested packets and tensor constructions, and compute the boundary control from the actual theta-derivative sequence. The cumulative reader also develops the relation-layer graph, derivative quotients, norm and Gram-volume identities, and conjugation/reflection-symmetric estimates. Spectral-sum constructions keep the relative variables through matrix weights and complete nilpotent fibres. The quantitative question is how the control form compares with the original arithmetic Gram matrix as the degree and tensor order grow; smallness of one matrix alone is not treated as the required relative estimate. The broader zeta programme 13-main-reader-425p.pdf supplies the surrounding literature reconstruction, CUE random-matrix calculations, arithmetic transforms and source-directed fluid calculations. It includes the all-axis Mellin calculation, complex axial branch points, moving analytic radius and endpoint-residue map for the stated source patch. Those results are described with their source assumptions and maps; they are not recast as a newly constructed zeta-zero witness or an independent proof of the imported fluid existence result. The motivation includes the use of weights in Deligne's Weil II . This programme works out its own analytic spaces, operators, metrics and comparison maps. The complete proofs retain their domains, signs, measures, scalar actions, local units and multiplicities. These are substantive calculations and research attempts, not a claim that an analogy by itself proves or disproves the Riemann hypothesis. Their manifests pin the exact revisions and file identities. items.summary: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

items.summary: Circular economy is the trend that has emerged as an urgent necessity for manufacturing companies trying to break the linear "take, make, dispose" production cycle. While there is a significant amount of research happening in the circularity domain, the body of knowledge is split and does not necessarily connect with other theories, concepts and with application in different industrial sectors. The aim of this study was to develop an integrated conceptual framework to overcome the existing ambiguities in the field of CE and to facilitate further research while synthesizing the various streams of research on the topic. Methods: The articles were systematically identified from Web of Science and Scopus databases, and then snowballing was performed, in compliance with the PRISMA guidelines, between 2010 and 2025, and resulted in the identification of 100 articles. A tripartite analytical technique based on the use of quantitative bibliometric analysis, qualitative bibliographic content analysis and conceptual mapping was used. Results: The major thematic clusters that emerged were: circular supply chains, design for circularity, industrial symbiosis, Industry 4.0 enablers, policy and governance, performance measurement. The key practices of CE were identified and categorized according to the 4R and 10R frameworks, reverse logistics, industrial symbiosis and digital support for resource recovery at the micro, meso and macro level. The analysis shows that there are organizational, financial, technological and regulatory challenges that remain unaddressed, and that there is a significant lack of empirical evidence on a larger scale. Conclusions: There is a coherent conceptual framework linking CE principles with supply chain operations and Industry 4.0 technologies in this review and it proposes a prioritized future research direction that covers eight critical knowledge gaps. Government, industry and academia receive practical guidance on how to speed circular transitions in manufacturing.

items.summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). items.summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. items.summary: This chapter explores the epistemic tensions faced by researchers, particularly those from formerly colonized countries in the Global South, caught between the demands of scientific neutrality and ethical engagement with the coloniality of knowledge. In dialogue with Critical Theory and decolonial thought, the chapter highlights epistemic resilience as a posture of resistance and reconstruction of meaning. The Haitian case study, through the heritage-based preservation of the memory of slavery, illustrates how cognitive justice can serve as a bridge between emancipatory rationality and the pluriversal horizon of decoloniality. Published as a chapter (pp. 239-257) of EDUCATORÉ. Educating and Reflecting for Resilient, Critically Aware Societies, Maria Grzegorzewska University Press, Warsaw.
items.title: Epistemological tensions and researcher resilience in a context of coloniality: navigating between neutrality and engagement

items.summary: Per-run results and analysis code behind every rate reported in the paper "How Credentials Leak from 'Safe' LLM Coding Agents: An Attack-Surface Measurement" (under review, Springer Cybersecurity). All measurements are the undefended baseline (no runtime judge, filter, or approval gate). items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted mathematical discovery, program search, and formal reasoning motivate a practical design question: how can a long-horizon open problem be reorganized into a broad, falsifiable, and evidence-accountable human–AI search? We present a prospective candidate-engineering framework, grounded in a source-bound retrospective Phase-I design case on arithmetic dynamical structures relevant to the Hilbert–Pólya programme. The paper does not claim a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a completed Hilbert–Pólya realization, or a spectral identification of Riemann zeros. The framework has three layers. In Layer 1, a mathematician fixes a mathematical origin, permitted data, and an admissible transformation class; the present case uses a prime-symbolic origin, whereas a new mathematician-supplied basic idea begins a new Layer-1 record. In Layer 2, mathematician and AI jointly draft and version-freeze an AGENTS.md contract specifying candidate identity, lineage, gates, controls, portfolio policy, and stopping rules. In Layer 3, bounded AI work returns a source-linked evidence handoff for mathematician review. The accompanying roadmap requires a single candidate to establish an endogenous arithmetic source, orbit/repetition ownership, and a same-object zeta or determinant before stronger analytic and operator obligations are considered. The case comprises one early exploration entry and five system-family sessions. Its P1 Wiki retains catalogued provenance records rather than a common score of completed papers, theorems, or Route advances. No source-bound top-level direction documents an integrated same-object A0+A1+A2 chain in one natural candidate. We therefore motivate a broader but lineage-filtered candidate portfolio, screened early for arithmetic, clock, and determinant ownership rather than assembled retrospectively from partial successes. The associated Wiki is a provenance and navigation resource designed to preserve positive local results, controls, scoped failures, and reuse boundaries for subsequent researchers.
items.title: AI-Guided Exploration of Arithmetic Dynamical Systems: Constraints, Failure Modes, and Search Strategies Toward Hilbert--Pólya Structures

items.summary: BanglaVLP-5K is a curated high-resolution image dataset of Bangladeshi vehicles and real-world traffic scenes, including images in which vehicle licence plates are visible. The dataset was developed to provide a reusable collection of real-world vehicle imagery from the Bangladeshi traffic environment for computer vision, intelligent transportation, image-analysis, and related research. The original image collection contained 4,993 images. All source images underwent a systematic technical and curation workflow including image-readability verification, file-integrity assessment, SHA-256 hashing, exact-duplicate analysis, perceptual near-duplicate and same-scene candidate identification, repeated-source-basename review, and conservative visual curation. Following the final curation stage, 4,955 images were retained for the public dataset, while 38 visually redundant near-identical images were excluded. The final dataset contains 4,955 technically readable images with 4,955 unique SHA-256 checksums. The median image resolution is approximately 2448 × 3264 pixels, corresponding to approximately 7.99 megapixels. The final image collection occupies approximately 14.52 GB. The dataset is distributed across five size-balanced image archives. Each archive contains an “images” directory holding the curated images and a “part_manifest.csv” file that provides the image identifiers, publication filenames, original filenames, file sizes, SHA-256 checksums, and archive-part information for the images contained in that archive. A separate metadata and documentation archive is also provided. It contains the complete final image manifest, image-level SHA-256 checksums, the dataset data dictionary, the Zenodo archive-part assignment, dataset summary statistics, final integrity-check results, the curation protocol, quality-control documentation, a dataset card, a repository file guide, and figures describing the dataset-preparation workflow and image-resolution distribution. Images in the public archives use standardized identifiers and filenames such as BDVLP_000001.jpg. Original source filenames are preserved in the metadata manifest for provenance and reproducibility. The image packaging procedure preserves the original source image bytes and does not resize or re-encode the images. BanglaVLP-5K is released as an annotation-free curated raw-image dataset. It does not include manually verified licence-plate bounding boxes, licence-plate character transcriptions, or manually verified vehicle-category ground-truth labels. Any automatically generated vehicle-category estimates present in the metadata are provided only as auxiliary technical descriptors and must not be interpreted as verified annotations or ground-truth labels. The dataset may be useful for computer vision research, vehicle and traffic-scene analysis, domain adaptation, transfer learning, image-quality and robustness studies, development and evaluation of image-processing methods, and the creation of future manually annotated derivative datasets for vehicle or licence-plate-related research. Users should consult the included README, dataset card, data dictionary, curation protocol, quality-control documentation, final image manifest, and SHA-256 checksum file before using the dataset.

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

No claim of quantum advantage is made; the artifacts are intended to support independent verification, methodological replication, and further investigation of QAOA-based cybersecurity investment optimization.

items.summary: This replication package contains the data, R scripts, figures, and documentation used in the study “Turkey–Greece Naval Procurement Rivalry, 1990–2025.” The study examines the temporal structure of naval procurement competition between Turkey and Greece using annual data for 1990–2025. The main empirical series are derived from the SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and SIPRI Transfer Register. Annual Ships Trend Indicator Value (TIV) data are used to measure international naval platform deliveries, while order-year information is used to distinguish procurement decisions from subsequent deliveries. World Bank World Development Indicators are used for the macroeconomic control variable. The analysis tests contemporaneous and 1–3-year lagged relationships between Greek and Turkish naval procurement. Robustness checks include Newey–West HAC standard errors, alternative bandwidths, leave-one-out tests, influential-year exclusions, winsorization, placebo leads, and multiple-testing corrections using the Benjamini–Hochberg, Holm, and Bonferroni procedures. All data preparation and statistical analyses were conducted in R. The results show that Turkish and Greek naval procurement processes are temporally connected rather than independent. The strongest delivery-to-delivery association appears at a two-year lag. Greek naval deliveries are also associated with Turkish international naval orders one year later, while reverse-direction models identify associations between Turkish deliveries and subsequent Greek international orders. The overall pattern is consistent with reciprocal and temporally clustered modernization cycles rather than a fixed one-way action–reaction process. The repository includes cleaned analytical datasets, R scripts, figures, a codebook, reproducibility documentation, citation metadata, and the manuscript. Raw proprietary or redistribution-restricted source files are not included; users should consult the original SIPRI and World Bank sources where applicable. Version 1.2 adds the reviewer-requested stationarity diagnostics, first-difference sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-programme-window-out tests. The revised package also includes updated regression outputs and the reviewer-revised manuscript. The main research design and core delivery-to-delivery finding remain unchanged.

items.summary: Overview  This repository contains the dataset, preprocessing pipeline, surrogate model training scripts, NSGA-II multi-objective optimization suite, and raw experimental outputs supporting the manuscript: "A Leakage-Controlled CatBoost–NSGA-II Framework for Concrete Mix Design: Evaluation Protocol and Strength-Floor Sensitivity" Abstract Traditional concrete mix design usually involves lengthy empirical trial-and-error procedures. This study proposes a CatBoost–NSGA-II framework for multi-objective optimisation of concrete mixes, including leakage-controlled evaluation, uncertainty-aware strength feasibility, repeated-run robustness, and strength-floor sensitivity analysis. To evaluate the surrogate models, a source-study-grouped evaluation protocol consisting of ten repeated train–test splits was employed. The compressive strength model obtained only moderate performance (R^2 = 0.654 ± 0.062), whereas the RCPT model exhibited unstable performance (R^2 = -1.01 ± 3.07) and was therefore not included in the optimisation constraints. An uncertainty-aware lower confidence bound was used for strength feasibility, and the buildability constraints were incorporated into NSGA-II. For the 40 MPa case, 20 separate runs resulted in a robust 15-member Pareto front with an 86.7% recurrence rate. The mixture chosen had estimated reductions of 50.0% in embodied carbon and 22.7% in material cost as compared with a baseline that had the same strength. Nevertheless, the benefits decreased as the strength floor was raised and became statistically no different from zero at 70 MPa. Experimental verification based on physical tests is necessary before the approach can be applied in practice. Repository Structure  * 1_data/: Processed concrete mix dataset (processed_dataset_1867_records.csv) and RCPT sub-dataset (rcpt_subset_203.csv).  * 2_code/: Python codebase including data_cleaner.py, train_catboost.py, nsga2_optimization.py, and run_full_pipeline.py.  * models/: Serialized .joblib CatBoost surrogate model binaries and uncertainty parameters.  * results/: Raw Pareto front outputs across 20 independent seed runs (pareto_front_seed_42.csv through seed_61.csv) and consolidated multi-run front metrics.  * Root: reproducibility_manifest.yaml, data_dictionary.csv, exclusion_log.csv, and main entrypoint run_all.py. Instructions for Reproducibility  * Extract concrete_mix_zenoda.zip.  * Install requirements: pip install -r 2_code/requirements.txt.  * Execute python run_all.py to re-run data cleaning, surrogate training, and multi-objective optimization.

items.summary: Research artifacts supporting the paper “Cybersecurity Investment Optimization Under Budget Constraints: From QUBO Formulation to Quantum Hardware”. This repository contains the source code, derived experimental instances, raw quantum measurement counts, QUBO/Ising models, QAOA execution outputs, transpiled-circuit metadata, backend information, job identifiers, and processed JSON/CSV results used to reproduce the experiments reported in the paper. The experiments implement an end-to-end cybersecurity investment optimization workflow based on a 0/1 Knapsack formulation transformed into QUBO and Ising representations and solved using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA). The experimental design includes ideal simulation with Qiskit AerSimulator, architecture-aware noisy emulation using FakeKingston, and execution on the real IBM Quantum ibm_kingston Heron r2 processor. The artifact set covers the 12-qubit reference benchmark, the 20-qubit Safeguard-level stress experiment, and the real-hardware scaling series at 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, and 156 logical qubits. For the scaling experiments, the decision variables beyond the original benchmark are explicitly constructed computational replicas used exclusively to evaluate circuit scaling, transpilation overhead, feasibility degradation, and real-QPU behavior; they must not be interpreted as distinct empirical cybersecurity controls. The repository preserves the information necessary to inspect and reproduce the experimental workflow, including optimized and transferred QAOA parameters, shot counts, sampled bitstrings, decoded cybersecurity portfolios, feasibility indicators, QUBO energies, circuit depths, gate counts, two-qubit gate counts, and real-hardware execution metadata. The public-evidence input dataset, CIS_MITRE_QAOA_Public_Evidence, is maintained separately on Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/andersonfpdossantos/cis-mitre-qaoa-public-evidence The dataset and these computational artifacts together provide the reproducibility package for the study. No claim of quantum advantage is made; the artifacts are intended to support independent verification, methodological replication, and further investigation of QAOA-based cybersecurity investment optimization.

items.summary: Whether a neural language model can report facts about its own computation is difficult to evaluate because an accurate report may be generated either from the realized runtime state or from a static simulation of the computation conditioned on the input and fixed parameters. We formalize this distinction and show that, under deterministic inference, an internal property of an unperturbed forward pass is not by itself sufficient to distinguish these mechanisms: the realized state is an exact deterministic function of the static input and parameters.  We introduce the Exogenous State Watermark (ESW), a controlled intervention protocol in which an externally sampled perturbation is injected into an intermediate representation while the model's observable next-token output is audited for greedy invariance. For the isolated watermark bit, the static information set has a 50% Bayes-optimal chance bound under the stated independence assumptions. For the counterfactual target, we evaluate unperturbed-state and runtime representations empirically on GPT-2 (124M parameters; width 768). In ESW-1A, a planted directional watermark becomes increasingly decodable as training examples grow relative to representation dimension, reaching 88.4% held-out accuracy at N/d=6.51 (cos θ = 0.9236), while a one-dimensional control reaches 100.0%. In an exploratory Oracle Ladder diagnostic, differential signals peak at Layer 8 before downstream attenuation. In the subsequent multi-seed paired-counterfactual benchmark (ESW-2B), an external nonlinear probe of intermediate runtime differences reaches approximately 0.62–0.63 AUROC, while the tested unperturbed-state baseline remains close to chance (0.507 AUROC) and a sample-label decoupled control remains at 0.546 AUROC. The paired bootstrap difference between the joint and runtime-only models includes zero (ΔAUROC = +0.012, 95% CI [-0.023, +0.047]), demonstrating that adding baseline activations provides no statistically detectable advantage over the runtime perturbation alone.  We interpret the experiments as empirical evidence for runtime-state-dependent decodability under the ESW intervention, not as evidence that GPT-2 possesses autonomous introspection, privileged self-report, consciousness, or subjective self-knowledge.
items.title: Runtime-State Watermarking in Transformers: A Controlled Protocol for Distinguishing Static Self-Simulation from Runtime-State Decodability

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).
tags: LLM agents; cyber deception; network security

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: The IMEB-Exo Synthetic Benchmark Dataset is an open and reproducible dataset developed for the analysis of passive upper-limb exoskeletons, occupational biomechanics, human–exoskeleton interaction, and multicriteria biomechanical decision support. It provides deterministic synthetic time-series data and derived biomechanical indicators designed to support methodological validation, sensitivity analysis, benchmarking, and reproducibility of the IMEB-Exo framework (Multicriteria Biomechanical Exposure Index for Exoskeletons). The dataset represents 24 virtual anthropometric models evaluated under three simulated occupational task scenarios and two experimental conditions: without exoskeleton assistance and with a passive upper-limb exoskeleton. The data structure enables comparisons between assisted and non-assisted conditions across multiple anthropometric profiles, task scenarios, and human–exoskeleton interface regions. The time-series dataset includes normal and tangential human–exoskeleton interface forces, estimated interface pressure when a technically defined contact area is available, shoulder and trunk kinematics, exoskeleton assistance torque, joint reaction variables, muscle activation surrogates, and cumulative biomechanical exposure indicators. Derived variables include peak and mean force, 95th-percentile force, root mean square (RMS) force, force–time integral, loading rate, time above an operational load threshold, peak counts, projected occupational exposure, CRITIC objective weights, TOPSIS results, IMEB-Exo scores, biomechanical criticality classes (CCB-Exo), and rankings of human–exoskeleton interface regions. The repository contains: • deterministic synthetic biomechanical time-series data; • interface-level and scenario-level metrics; • IMEB-Exo scores and regional rankings; • CRITIC objective weights and TOPSIS outputs; • metadata for 24 virtual anthropometric models; • task and scenario definitions; • human–exoskeleton interface definitions and contact-area specifications; • generation parameters; • a structured SQLite database; • CSV and compressed CSV datasets; • Python scripts for dataset generation and IMEB-Exo calculation; • data dictionary and schema documentation; • SHA-256 checksums and file inventory; • representative figures and data excerpts; • reproducibility documentation in English and Portuguese. The dataset is intended for researchers working with occupational biomechanics, passive occupational exoskeletons, wearable robotics, ergonomic risk assessment, musculoskeletal modelling, multicriteria decision analysis (MCDA/MCDM), decision-support systems, synthetic biomechanical datasets, and reproducible computational research. Methodological notice: the dataset is synthetic and deterministic. The generated variables reproduce the expected structure and behaviour of an OpenSim-oriented musculoskeletal simulation workflow but do not constitute experimentally measured human data and must not be interpreted as direct outputs from an executed OpenSim simulation. The dataset should therefore be used as a methodological benchmark for algorithm development, reproducibility testing, sensitivity analysis, multicriteria modelling, and computational workflow validation rather than as experimental evidence of human biomechanical responses. The dataset was developed within the project “Multicriteria Methods for the Analysis of Monitored Data in the Use of Passive Upper-Limb Exoskeletons”, supported by FAEPEX / University of Campinas (UNICAMP), Grant No. 70262-26.

items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .
items.title: The Cost of Reliability in Optimal Magnetization Switching: A Longitudinal-Field Front for Van der Waals Magnets
